es: Rebatir con tacto y firmeza usando atenuantes, refuerzos y frases hendidas en un texto argumentativo.

teaching.en: What matters is the cost, not the colour of the new benches.
teaching.es: Lo que importa es el coste, no el color de los bancos nuevos.
teaching.explanationEs: What + sujeto + verbo + is + X pone el foco en X; aquí, en el coste.

the colour of the new benches.

teaching.en: It is the cost that many families overlook.
teaching.es: Es el coste lo que muchas familias pasan por alto.
teaching.explanationEs: It is + X + that + verbo: en inglés se usa that, no what, tras el elemento destacado.
teaching.audioText: It is the cost that many families overlook.

teaching.en: The plan is arguably the cheapest option, but it is not the fairest.
teaching.es: El plan es posiblemente la opción más barata, pero no la más justa.
teaching.explanationEs: Arguably atenúa: presentas la afirmación como defendible, no como un hecho.
segments: The plan is arguably the cheapest option,
but it is not the fairest.

teaching.en: The fee is undoubtedly a problem for families with three children.
teaching.es: La cuota es sin duda un problema para las familias con tres hijos.
teaching.explanationEs: Undoubtedly refuerza: lo usas cuando tienes pruebas o estás seguro.
segments: The fee is undoubtedly a problem
teaching.audioText: The fee is undoubtedly a problem for families with three children.

teaching.en: That is a reasonable point; what I oppose is the timing.
teaching.es: Es un punto razonable; a lo que me opongo es al momento elegido.
teaching.explanationEs: Concedes primero (reasonable point) y destacas después lo que realmente rebates.

teaching.audioText: That is a reasonable point; what I oppose is the timing.

teaching.en: What is essential is a fair price for every family.
teaching.es: Lo esencial es un precio justo para cada familia.
teaching.explanationEs: Essential refuerza lo que consideras imprescindible y la frase hendida lo coloca en primer plano.
teaching.audioText: What is essential is a fair price for every family.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención: concesión, refutación con frase hendida y cierre.

answer.text: In my view, pupils should clean their classroom once a week. Admittedly, it takes time away from lessons, and some parents will say that cleaning is the job of the school. That is a reasonable point, but what matters is the habit we build. It is the pupils who use the room every day, and it is undoubtedly fairer that all of us look after it. Arguably, a clean room also helps us study better, because nobody likes to work among rubbish. Another reason is the cost: it is the cost of extra staff that the school would pay otherwise, and that money could buy books instead. Clearly, ten minutes on Friday is not too much to ask. To conclude, what is essential is that we share the work, because the classroom belongs to all of us.

I believe pupils should clean their classroom every week. I concede that it takes time from lessons, and some parents think the school should do it. That is a reasonable point, but what matters is the habit we learn. It is the pupils who use the room all day, so it is undoubtedly fair that we look after it. Arguably, a clean room helps us study, because nobody concentrates well among rubbish. It is also the cost that the school would save, and that money could buy books for the library. Clearly, ten minutes on Friday is a small price to pay. In conclusion, what is essential is that we share the work, and the whole class benefits.

feedback.es: Una respuesta completa concede, rebate con What matters is… o It is… that, matiza con arguably y refuerza con undoubtedly, y cierra.

origin.text: Debate escolar: ¿deben los alumnos limpiar su aula una vez por semana? Defiendes que sí. Concede que se pierde tiempo de clase. Rebate con frases hendidas (lo que importa es el hábito; es el coste lo que el colegio pagaría). Usa un atenuante (arguably) y un refuerzo (undoubtedly). Cierra con una conclusión.
